title: Fractions, Units and Necessary Conditions
topics: Fractions describe selected equal parts of one whole
Denominators name units; numerators count selected units
Equivalent fractions via multiplying by the same positive integer
Checking fraction reasoning with units and original quantities
conditions: Fractions must refer to the same whole before their quantities can be compared.
Equivalent fractions require multiplying both numerator and denominator by the same positive integer.
If the original wholes differ, first describe their sizes instead of treating the fractions alone as a sufficient comparison.
quotes: Fractions must refer to the same whole before their quantities can be compared.
Equivalent fractions represent the same quantity: multiplying both numerator and denominator by the same positive integer changes the partition without changing the quantity.
uncertainties: The source gives the addition example 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6 but does not derive how to find sixths in general.
The source requires labeling the whole and equal-sized parts in a drawn model but does not specify further model conventions.
